agent: home yield (OpenHOI3: a later start's home production of resources on occupied land)
question: Why a new game's metal, energy and rare materials made at home fall short of the 1939 and 1941 start saves for Germany and China, whose joined land includes occupied provinces, while the 1936 start agrees

addresses.name: CMapProvince::ResourceYield
addresses.signature: int* __fastcall CMapProvince::ResourceYield(CMapProvince* province@ESI, int* out@stack:4, int goods@stack:8)
addresses.revises: the comment only: it now names what the two tables hold, says the two multiplications are truncated in turn (technology first), and records that the country table has fuel's and money's modifiers the wrong way round; name, signature and confidence unchanged
addresses.comment: What a province yields of one good in a day. Read whole 2026-11-15. `out` = current_producing[goods] (+0x270 + goods*4); nothing more where that is 0. For metal (4), rare materials (6) and energy (5) only: out = out * (1000 + the controller's technology_status +0xAC / +0xB0 / +0xB4) / 1000, 64-bit, truncated (0xB99980). Then for every good: f = 1000 + province modifier[T1[goods]] + controller modifier[T2[goods]] + province modifier 85 (MODIFIER_LOCAL_RESOURCES) + controller modifier 84 (MODIFIER_GLOBAL_RESOURCES), f = 0 where negative (jns), out = out * f / 1000, truncated. The controller is the province's controller tag (+0x334) through CCountryTag::GetCountry, its modifier values at +0xDA8; the province's at +0x114. T1 (0x1713F40, by goods 0..6) = 26 LOCAL_SUPPLIES, 28 LOCAL_FUEL, 30 LOCAL_MONEY, 18 LOCAL_CRUDE_OIL, 22 LOCAL_METAL, 20 LOCAL_ENERGY, 24 LOCAL_RARE_MATERIALS; T2 (0x1713F5C) = 27 GLOBAL_SUPPLIES, **31 GLOBAL_MONEY for fuel and 29 GLOBAL_FUEL for money** - the two swapped against T1 - 19, 23, 21, 25. So the four modifiers **add** and scale the yield once, after the technology; an occupied province at non_core's -0.5 under +10% laws yields 0.6 of itself, not 0.55. Measured: with this rule OpenHOI3's home production of every resource is the save's for every country in the 1936, 1939.9.1, 1941.6.22 and 1941.12.11 start saves - Germany's metal 332.084 at 1941.6.22, where multiplying gave 312.093. Callers: CCountry::CollectDailyProduction, ProvinceView_ResourceText. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x4A6EB0..0x4A6FAA (scripts/disasm.py): the tech multiply at 0x4A6F24..0x4A6F3F, the table loads at 0x4A6F41 and 0x4A6F65, modifiers +0x2A8 (85) and +0x2A0 (84) at 0x4A6F7B and 0x4A6F85, the jns floor at 0x4A6F8D, the second multiply at 0x4A6F93. The two tables read out of .rdata (7 dwords each) and named through ghidra/modifierIds.json. Measured beside four start saves: Germany's metal/energy/rare 332.084/1122.471/80.743 at 1941.6.22 and 382.316/1304.861/93.899 at 1941.12.11, China's 44.990/134.950/16.940 at 1939.9.1, each to the thousandth, and every country's resources in the 1936 save still the save's. Shown wrong by a province with a local_resources modifier whose saved yield is the product of (1 + local) and (1 + global) rather than their sum.
